newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels said ready to free soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels said ready to free soldiers.

text.p: Up to 20 of the 60 Colombian soldiers captured by leftist guerrillas eight months ago could be freed soon, a journalist who interviewed one captive said on Wednesday.

Radionet radio network reporter Camilo Higuera, the first person to make direct contact with the soldiers since they were seized in the jungles of southern Colombia on Aug. 30, said guerrilla leaders told him a group of between 15 and 20 prisoners would be released on Thursday afternoon.

The release could mark the beginning of the end of one of Latin America's longest-running hostages sagas, although it is one that has received far less media attention that the seizure of the Japanese embassy residence in Lima.
In the interview, the soldier pleaded with the government to demilitarize the area where he and his companions are being held to make way for their release.
President Ernesto Samper said the government would do "everything in its power" to secure the soldiers' safe return.

The 60 soldiers, many of them recruits, were captured when Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia FARC rebels overran a military base in Putumayo province. Another 27 soldiers died in the attack, one of the most humiliating defeats inflicted on the army in more than three decades of guerrilla warfare.
